text1: Trapped at the frozen edge of the primary's gravity well, an unusually dense atmospheric blanket and hyperactive mantle currents trap enough core heat to sustain a temperate surface. Without solar weathering, geological evolution is driven entirely by internal dynamics, leaving crustal stability and mineral distribution wildly unpredictable.
notes: Rogue Planets mod: Nocturnal World description

text1: An exceptionally rare paradise world boasting perfect atmospheric balance, stable biomes, and virtually limitless agricultural yields. However, the world's delicate planetary biosphere is remarkably fragile; heavy industrialization, surface mining, and mass manufacturing risk triggering rapid ecological collapse, restricting development strictly to low-impact agricultural cultivation.

The world's hyper-delicate planetary ecosystem prohibits heavy industrial zoning. Surface mining, refining, fuel production, and heavy industry cannot be constructed, preserving the biosphere for low-impact agriculture.

A carbon-rich gas giant, banded in dark hydrocarbon haze. Its upper atmosphere carries unusually high concentrations of methane, ethane, and heavy organic compounds, layered by temperature and easy to skim and separate. Unbreathable and crushed by immense pressure below, it is a dream for heavy industrial chemistry.

A severe localized distortion in the planet's space-time continuum causes subjective surface time to flow at an accelerated rate relative to the surrounding stellar system. Offworld logistics and cargo transfers complete almost instantaneously, dramatically boosting accessibility. However, physical materials endure decades of structural wear and entropic decay in mere standard months and doubling facility upkeep costs. Furthermore, drydocked and stationed warships suffer extreme relativistic fatigue and sensor desynchronization across the shear boundary, guaranteeing deployed vessels are decrepit.

A colossal, hellish world locked in perpetual geological upheaval. Its crust is a restless mosaic of grinding plates and open magma seas, venting superheated toxic gases into a choking, ash-laden atmosphere that blots out nearly all starlight. Crushing gravity, lethal radiation, constant meteoric bombardment and planet-wide superstorms make any surface presence all but unsurvivable.

By every known law of stellar physics, a star cannot burn this color. No fusion cycle in any survey database produces a violet spectrum, and the Domain's own models, when fed the readings, return only errors. The light is steady, deep and wrong, and it settles on every hull, cloud and ocean in the system like a held breath. Survey crews report instruments that disagree with one another, and a persistent sense of being watched from the far side of the glow. The charts list it as a white dwarf. The charts are mistaken.

An orbital habitat of Domain pattern, intact in every particular. Air handlers cycle, lights burn in the corridors, and tables are laid for a meal in the mess. There are no people, no bodies and no records of any. Every viewport faces the star, and every chair in the common room is turned to face the viewports.

The survey ship's hull is thick with a century of dust and its transponder is still broadcasting, one phrase on a loop. The registry lists it as lost in a different sector, in a different decade. Its last log entry is dated tomorrow.

A dense, dark body drifting through the ring dust, absorbing nearly every wavelength your instruments throw at it. It has no entry in any catalogue. Close up, its surface is smooth and faintly warm, and it appears to be exactly as wide as your fleet.

The fragments of the signal were never a warning. They were directions. At their meeting point sits a vault of no recognizable make, its door already open, with contents arranged as though for a guest who had been expected for a long time.

The bed of a vanished ocean. Whatever seas once covered this world boiled or bled away long ago, leaving a planet-wide crust of halite and other evaporite salts, split into endless polygonal plates by cycles of heat and frost. The last brine lakes shelter in the deepest basins, ringed by bands of mineral deposits and stained pink and red by hardy halophile microbes. The thin, salt-laden air scours every exposed surface, and the poisoned ground will grow almost nothing.
notes: Rogue Planets mod: Halite World description

text1: Once a gas giant, now a corpse. Drifting too close to its primary, this world had its entire hydrogen and helium envelope boiled off and blown into space over millions of years, leaving only the core: a vast, hyper-dense ball of compressed iron, nickel and rock that was never meant to see light. Crushing gravity holds everything to the surface, the dayside glows along its deepest rifts, and the crust is threaded with metal in quantities no ordinary world could hold.
notes: Rogue Planets mod: Chthonian World description

text1: Too massive to be called a planet and too small to have ever become a star, this super-Jupiter is still shedding the heat of its own formation. Beneath decks of iron-droplet and silicate cloud that rain molten metal into the depths, the interior glows a dull magenta in the infrared, bright enough that the night side never truly goes dark. Its gravity well is immense, and its storms dwarf entire worlds.
notes: Rogue Planets mod: Sub-Brown Dwarf description

text1: This world was not always frozen. Ancient coastlines and mountain ranges can still be traced beneath a single unbroken sheet of ice that covers every ocean and continent from pole to pole, a runaway glaciation that reflected away so much light it could never thaw. Only the highest peaks break through the ice, and near the equator thin dark leads of young sea ice hint at the liquid ocean that may still lie trapped beneath.
notes: Rogue Planets mod: Snowball World description

text1: Something broke this world. Whether a collision, a weapon or forces older than the Domain, the blow split the crust into drifting continental plates and tore whole regions away into orbit, where they still tumble alongside the wounded core in a cloud of rubble. The rifts between the plates glow with exposed mantle, quakes never stop, and the debris rains back down without end. For those willing to endure it, the planet's insides now lie open to the sky.
notes: Rogue Planets mod: Sundered World description
